correctness.rationale: For all connected weight designs, log(det grounded Laplacian) is strictly concave in the full edge vector because the grounded edge-incidence map determines each edge weight. The unique design must respect the stabilizer of the exceptional edge. Three conductance classes a,b,c yield nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues s=2a+(n-2)b, nb, and t=2b+(n-2)c with multiplicity n-3, giving exact tau=b*s*t^(n-3). Euler homogeneity fixes lambda=(n-1)/B. Full KKT equations solve to the displayed positive a,b,c for r<(n-1)/(n-2) and to a=0, b=2B/(n-1)^2, c=2B(n-3)/((n-1)^2(n-2)) otherwise. At a=0 the derivative 2/((n-2)b) <=lambda r holds exactly above the threshold; uniqueness follows including equality. Independently computed grounded minors, budgets and every original edge-gradient KKT condition in 16 exact rational test cases; tests corroborate the all-n argument.
residual_risks: Uniqueness uses injectivity of edge weights into grounded Laplacian; this holds for simple K_n, not generally for parallel edges.
No integer trial counts, multiple abnormal prices, or edgewise upper bounds are considered.

originality.rationale: Osting–Brune–Osher derive general Laplacian D-optimal spanning-tree objectives, and Harman–Benková provide general constrained D-optimal equivalence/KKT machinery. Neither inspected result evaluates the full K_n single-edge price allocation and sharp (n-1)/(n-2) active-set threshold. The calculation is a specialization of known tools but the all-parameter explicit design and one-edge support transition are not mechanically stated in inspected literature.
residual_risks: A classical complete-block-graph optimal-design calculation may give equivalent exact weights.
Generic KKT machinery itself and determinant equivalence are not novel.

value.rationale: An exact cost premium above 1+1/(n-2) deletes one pairwise comparison entirely from the determinant-optimal fully connected information network, while all other edges remain active. The threshold and all weights for every n and positive budget/price are natural experimental-design invariants and identify a sharp support phase transition, rather than a selected numerical instance.
residual_risks: Continuous conductance allocation is an approximation to discrete experimental budgets.

final_claim: For K_n, n>=4, budget B>0 and one exceptional edge price r>0, the unique spanning-tree determinant maximizer deletes exactly that edge iff r>=(n-1)/(n-2); both regimes have the stated three-class closed-form conductances and maximum.
limitations: One exceptional edge price, all other prices equal; unrestricted nonnegative continuous conductances.
No claims for multi-price or discrete design.
